name: Park Hyatt Changbaishan
positioning: Mountain-slope resort in Changbaishan International Resort, with rooms spread over villas, traditional Chinese decor, an outdoor hot mineral pool and a forest-set spa
best_for: Skiers and mountain travelers who want to stay close to the ski slopes and Changbaishan West Slope
Families or groups wanting large suites with kitchens in a villa setting

facts.text: The resort is on the mountain slopes in Changbaishan International Resort.
The hotel is adjacent to the main pedestrian walk of the resort.
The hotel is close to ski slopes, restaurants and attractions.
Changbaishan West Slope is 1.63 kilometers from the hotel.
Nearby cultural attractions include Jinjiang Wooden Village and the Saman Culture Museum.
Guest rooms feature elements of traditional Chinese decor.
Standard guest rooms have a daybed, separate work area, espresso machine, and a bathroom with double sinks, heated floors and TV.
The Park Executive Suite has a separate living room, dining room and kitchen.
The Living Room on level 1 is the all-day dining venue, serving Western and Chinese comfort food for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
The fitness center is open 24 hours, with cardio equipment, weight machines and free weights.
Meeting rooms are residential in style, with natural light, outdoor terraces and modern audiovisual equipment.
Free self-parking is available for hotel guests on basement levels 1 and 2.

highlights.text: The hotel has an outdoor hot mineral pool.
The Spa at Park Hyatt Changbaishan is set in the dense virgin forests of the mountain.
At the Living Room, guests are encouraged to talk to the butlers or chefs directly about what they feel like eating, rather than order from a menu.
Rooms are spread over 10 villas, which suits family gatherings or large conferences.
The Living Room has views of the ski slopes and surrounding mountains.

considerations.text: Changbaishan Airport is 17.1 kilometers from the hotel.
The hotel recommends local mapping apps such as Gaode Map or Baidu Map for getting around in mainland China.
WhataHotel notes the remote mountain location and that access can depend on the weather.
